sources.title: How a Pareto answer gets made
sources.evidence: Explains a composite system that selects frontier and open models for a request and combines their outputs. Explicitly says model composition can change. Does not disclose a fixed member list, aggregate learned/active counts, or one dense/MoE network architecture.

sources.title: Unbiased terms defining Pareto and its license
sources.evidence: Defines Pareto as the company proprietary blended AI model, combining outputs from underlying models obtained through company arrangements. Section 2(c) grants use through the service and permits composition changes. This is a hosted proprietary service, not a published Pareto checkpoint license.

sources.title: About Unbiased
sources.evidence: Identifies Circuit & Chisel as the company building Unbiased and Pareto as its first model. Supports retaining the Unbiased product/developer brand.

sources.title: Original Union Alpha release and confirmed Pareto identity
sources.evidence: The original distributor explicitly dates public release September 16,2026, states that Union Alpha was developed/operated by Unbiased and revealed as Pareto, and records text/image input, text output and 262144 context. The free stealth period is over. This establishes public preview availability before the September 17 named listing.

sources.title: Pareto 26.10 release hub identifying the earlier 26.9 version
sources.evidence: Explicitly identifies Union Alpha as later revealed to be Pareto 26.9. Separately states that the current pareto default selects 26.10 and that pareto-26.9 remains available. The new 1M context belongs to 26.10, not the original September record.

sources.title: Exact Pareto 26.9 endpoint metadata
sources.evidence: Unbiased endpoint unbiased/pareto-26.9-20260917 documents 262144 context and 131072 max completion, text/image input and text output, tools and tool_choice with auto supported. Current provider slug creation is October 13; it is not the first public release date.

sources.title: Current resolution of the original unversioned provider id
sources.evidence: The frozen unversioned path now returns id ~unbiased/pareto-latest, name Pareto Latest, description that it redirects to the latest Pareto family model, and no endpoints. The original September 26.9 release must not be reinterpreted as a newly released 26.10 checkpoint.

sources.title: Unbiased product changes and model alias history
sources.evidence: October 1 entry distinguishes opt-in 26.10-preview from the then-default pareto. October 15 entry moves pareto to 26.10 and preserves 26.9. September entries show earlier platform/API operation but do not identify an earlier public release day for the exact 26.9 revision.

sources.title: Public Pareto API specification
sources.evidence: Documents OpenAI/Anthropic-format requests, tool definitions and assistant tool_calls with text responses. No dedicated public reasoning control is declared in the core specification. This absence does not prove the composite lacks reasoning ability.

sources.title: Current Pareto 26.10 model card, checked for older model disclosures
sources.evidence: The current card reports comparison scores explicitly labeled Pareto 26.9 but no parameter count, active count or fixed underlying architecture for 26.9. Current 26.10 benchmark results and rates are not transferred to the original release.

sources.title: Developer evaluation harness cascade result types
sources.evidence: Optional result fields include cascade stage, escalation, classifier tier, agreement method and finalModel. This is generic evaluation instrumentation, not a deployment configuration or proof of26.9 constituent identities/counts. The harness MIT license does not license hosted Pareto weights.

sources.title: October 1 launch notes describing the prior Pareto 26.9 stealth trial
sources.evidence: The developer says it put Pareto 26.9 on OpenRouter, OpenCode and Cloudflare AI Gateway under a made-up name two weeks earlier. Corroborates the original 26.9 identity and earlier public trial, separate from the October 26.10 preview.

sources.title: Union Alpha operator reveal post
sources.evidence: Direct access returned403. Not used as independently accessed evidence; the accessible original distributor and developer release pages establish identity and public-preview date.

name.note: Add the original release version to distinguish the frozen September model from the mutable latest alias and October 26.10 releases.

developer.note: Retain the developer/product brand; its legal operator is Circuit & Chisel.

family.note: The developer versions the Pareto family as 26.9 and 26.10.

release_date.note: Earliest explicit public availability is the September 16 Union Alpha stealth preview, whose identity is confirmed by the distributor and developer. September 17 is the named Pareto listing/reveal; October 13 is the later versioned-provider slug. Earlier generic platform changes do not establish a release date for this exact revision.

open_weights.note: Proprietary hosted composite with service-use rights; no single released Pareto weight artifact. Public constituent models or the MIT evaluation harness do not make Pareto itself open-weight.

license.note: Descriptive classification explicitly supported by the developer service terms. Do not copy licenses of undisclosed constituent models or the public evaluation code.

parameters_b.note: No fixed 26.9 member list or aggregate learned-parameter count is disclosed in the accessed mechanism page, later comparison card, release notes or developer harness. Several models are combined; do not turn unverified membership speculation into a total.

active_parameters_b.note: No aggregate active count or per-request accounting convention is disclosed for this changing composite. A count from one guessed constituent would not describe Pareto.

architecture.note: System-level design is a multi-model blend, not a disclosed single dense, MoE or hybrid neural checkpoint. Underlying network identities and architectures are undisclosed; combining model outputs is not evidence of neural mixture-of-experts routing. Generic cascade harness types do not identify the exact production 26.9 stack.

context_window.note: Exact documented hosted 26.9 limit. Retain 262144; the later 26.10 one-million-token window belongs to a different release. This is an endpoint contract, not an inferred shared constituent positional limit.

modalities.note: Original stealth and exact 26.9 endpoint both document native text/image requests and text responses. Server tools or later product integrations do not add output modalities.

reasoning.note: Neither absent reasoning controls nor benchmark scores establish a binary reasoning-mode claim for 26.9. Clear unsupported false; the inspected primary materials do not define this capability flag.

tool_call.note: The exact 26.9 provider endpoint accepts tools and auto tool_choice; developer API documents returned assistant tool_calls. This verifies supported function-calling interface, not a reliability score.

description.value: Unbiased's proprietary composite model that combines outputs from multiple language models. This entry describes the original Pareto 26.9 release.
description.note: State the documented system design and version; avoid unsupported comparative performance or a single-checkpoint implication.

patch.notes: This record describes Pareto 26.9, publicly available as Union Alpha on September 16, 2026. The unversioned alias later moved to 26.10. Pareto is a proprietary hosted blend whose model composition can change; a fixed member list, aggregate parameter counts and a single neural architecture are undisclosed. The 262144-token context is the documented 26.9 service limit. Reasoning-mode support is unverified.

summary: Distinguishes the original Pareto 26.9 release from its mutable alias, corrects earliest public availability to the September 16 Union Alpha preview, adds Pareto family and explicit proprietary license, and clears unsupported reasoning=false. Confirms 262144 hosted context, text/image input, text output and tool calls. Parameter counts and constituent architectures remain undisclosed for the changing multi-model blend; no single-model count or MoE classification is invented.
